config.title: useSyncExternalStore

intro.title: useSyncExternalStore
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that displays a real-time counter, learning how to integrate external state into Angular's reactive system. You'll use the useSyncExternalStore pattern, a concept for subscribing to and synchronizing with external data sources like browser APIs or third-party libraries. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and RxJS Observables to handle the subscription logic. By the end, you'll understand how to keep your UI in sync with external state changes efficiently and reactively.
intro.usecase: In real Angular applications, useSyncExternalStore is essential for synchronizing UI components with external data sources like WebSocket connections, browser APIs, or third-party libraries. You'll see this pattern in live dashboards that display real-time stock prices or IoT sensor data, where components must react instantly to external updates. It's also used in collaborative tools like shared document editors where cursor positions or user presence indicators update continuously. Developers implement this to ensure their components stay in sync with rapidly changing external state without manual subscription management.

objectives: Initialize a custom store with state and subscription logic
Implement a service that exposes the store and its methods
Configure a component to subscribe to external store changes
Apply the useSyncExternalStore pattern to synchronize component state
Manipulate store state through dedicated action methods
Render component UI that reflects the current synchronized state
Integrate store updates with Angular's change detection system

steps.title: Import Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Add imports for Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple Angular core features
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component file will have the necessary Angular core imports for creating a component with lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing all three: Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect. You need to import Component, OnInit, and OnDestroy from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class with Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator. Include an empty template string in the decorator metadata.
steps.hint: Use the imported Component decorator to define the component class. The template can be an empty string for now.

successCriteria: AppComponent class is created with @Component decorator containing template: ''
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created the AppComponent class with the @Component decorator and an empty template string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AppComponent class with @Component decorator is not correctly defined. Check the syntax and ensure the template is an empty string.

steps.title: Implement external store subscription logic in ngOnInit
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add the ngOnInit lifecycle method to subscribe to an external store and update a component property.
steps.hint: Use ngOnInit() { } to define the method. Inside, create a subscription to a mock store and update a property like 'storeValue'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method is added to the AppComponent class with subscription logic to an external store.
successCriteria: ngOnInit method is defined in AppComponent, contains subscription logic, and updates a component property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added ngOnInit, but ensure it contains subscription logic that updates a component property like 'storeValue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method is missing or doesn't contain subscription logic. Add ngOnInit() { } with store subscription code inside.

steps.title: Implement cleanup logic in ngOnDestroy
steps.instruction: Add the ngOnDestroy method to your AppComponent class to unsubscribe from the store subscription and prevent memory leaks.
steps.hint: Implement the ngOnDestroy lifecycle hook method and call unsubscribe() on your storeSubscription property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will properly clean up the subscription when destroyed, preventing memory leaks.
successCriteria: ngOnDestroy method is implemented and calls unsubscribe() on storeSubscription
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added ngOnDestroy, but make sure you're calling unsubscribe() on the storeSubscription property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnDestroy method is missing or doesn't properly unsubscribe from the store subscription.

steps.title: Define external store and its getSnapshot function
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, define a simple external store object with a state property and a getSnapshot function that returns the current state.
steps.hint: Create a property called 'store' with a 'state' value and a 'getSnapshot' method that returns this state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have a 'store' property containing an object with 'state' and 'getSnapshot' members.
successCriteria: A 'store' object is defined with a 'state' property and a 'getSnapshot' function that returns the state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your store object has both a 'state' property and a 'getSnapshot' function that returns that state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store definition is missing or incomplete. Remember to create an object with 'state' and 'getSnapshot' properties inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Define subscribe function for the external store
steps.instruction: Add a subscribe method to your external store object that accepts a listener callback function and returns an unsubscribe function.
steps.hint: The subscribe method should store the listener in an array and return a function that removes it from the array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The external store object now has a subscribe method that manages listener callbacks.
successCriteria: The externalStore object contains a subscribe method that accepts a listener function and returns an unsubscribe function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a subscribe method, but make sure it returns an unsubscribe function that removes the listener.
steps.feedbackWrong: The subscribe method is missing or doesn't follow the expected pattern. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Initialize component state with store snapshot
steps.instruction: In the ngOnInit method, initialize the storeValue property with the current snapshot from externalStore.getSnapshot()
steps.hint: Set this.storeValue equal to the result of calling this.externalStore.getSnapshot() inside ngOnInit
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's storeValue property will be initialized with the current value from the external store when the component loads
successCriteria: storeValue is initialized in ngOnInit using externalStore.getSnapshot()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling getSnapshot() on the externalStore object and assigning the result to storeValue inside ngOnInit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The storeValue property needs to be initialized in ngOnInit using the getSnapshot() method from externalStore. Try setting this.storeValue = this.externalStore.getSnapshot() inside the ngOnInit method.

steps.title: Add template to display the current state value
steps.instruction: Update the component's template to display the current storeValue using Angular interpolation.
steps.hint: In the @Component decorator's template property, add a paragraph element with double curly braces containing storeValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now shows the current storeValue when rendered.
successCriteria: The template property contains interpolation syntax {{ storeValue }} inside an HTML element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using double curly braces {{ }} around storeValue in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display storeValue. Add a paragraph or other element with {{ storeValue }} interpolation.

steps.title: Add increment button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element to the component's template that displays 'Increment' and has a click handler that calls a method to update the external store's state.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding in Angular to call a method when the button is clicked. You'll need to create a method in your component class that modifies the store's state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include a button that triggers a method to update the external store when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element exists in template with (click) binding
Click handler method is defined in component class
Method contains logic to update store state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the button, but make sure it has a proper (click) binding and the handler method is defined in the component class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or click handler is missing. Add a button element with (click)="methodName()" and define the corresponding method in your component class.

steps.title: Implement increment handler to update store
steps.instruction: In the AppComponent class, implement an increment method that updates the external store's state and triggers listeners.
steps.hint: Add a method that modifies the store's state and calls any subscribed listeners. You can update a local variable representing the store state and then notify listeners.
steps.expectedOutcome: The increment method updates the store's state and triggers listeners, enabling the component to sync with the updated state.
successCriteria: The AppComponent has an increment method that modifies the store state and notifies listeners.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but ensure it updates the store state and triggers listeners. Check the analogous example.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment method is missing or doesn't update the store state and notify listeners. Review the instruction and try again.
